introH2: 🏝️ What kind of stays does Koh Phi Phi in Krabi have, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Koh Phi Phi is one of the defining images of the Krabi sea — steep limestone cliffs, clear emerald water, and Maya Bay, which the whole world wants to see at least once · what many people don't realise is that the entire island has no roads and no cars; you can only reach it by boat — take the ferry to Tonsai Pier, then a longtail or resort boat out to your beach · the accommodation on the island splits into two clear moods — the Tonsai–Loh Dalum zone is the main village, lively and walkable with restaurants and nightlife, while Laem Tong, Loh Bagao, Long Beach and Loh Moo Dee are the quiet side, needing a boat transfer but trading it for privacy · we've ranked this list by real guest review scores, and on Phi Phi the stays people love most tend to be laid-back beachfront bungalows that match the island's rhythm, rather than big high-priced resorts · this article rounds up 8 Koh Phi Phi stays we've reviewed in depth, giving both the good points and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites with direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Koh Phi Phi has no roads and no cars; you can reach it by ferry from Phuket, Krabi or Ao Nang, about 1.5–2 hrs, landing at Tonsai Pier, then a longtail or resort boat out to your beach · the Tonsai–Loh Dalum zone = the main village, walkable, with restaurants and lively nightlife, drag your bag straight from the pier · Laem Tong · Loh Bagao · Long Beach · Loh Moo Dee = quiet and calm, needing a longtail/resort boat transfer, ideal for relaxing and honeymoons · Long Beach can be walked back to Tonsai along the shore at low tide · we recommend a waterproof, easy-to-drag bag, since some beaches mean wading through shallow water getting on and off the boat.

noteHtml: 📌 Note: all prices are approximate starting rates from the standard-room range and may change by date and season — we recommend checking real prices and comparing 3 sites before every booking · the scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms · Koh Phi Phi has no roads and no cars; you can get in and out by ferry from Phuket, Krabi or Ao Nang (~1.5–2 hrs), landing at Tonsai Pier, then a longtail/resort boat out to your beach, so pack a bag that's waterproof and easy to drag, since some beaches mean wading through shallow water getting on and off the boat · the Tonsai–Loh Dalum zone is the lively main village, while Laem Tong, Loh Bagao, Long Beach and Loh Moo Dee are quiet and calm, good for relaxing · high season (November–April) brings calm seas, fine weather and clear water for snorkelling, but higher prices and rooms that fill fast, so book ahead · article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers often ask about staying on Koh Phi Phi, Krabi

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Koh Phi Phi, do you have to take a boat?
faq.a: By boat only · Koh Phi Phi has no roads and no cars, reached by ferry from Phuket, Krabi or Ao Nang, about 1.5–2 hrs, landing at Tonsai Pier · if your stay is in the Tonsai–Loh Dalum zone you can walk or drag your bag straight there, but if it's at Laem Tong, Loh Bagao, Long Beach or Loh Moo Dee, you have to take a longtail or resort boat onward (some resorts have a free shuttle boat, so check when booking)

faq.q: ❓ Which zone of Koh Phi Phi should I stay in, the lively village or a quiet beach?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style · the Tonsai–Loh Dalum zone is the main village, lively and walkable with restaurants and nightlife, drag your bag straight from the pier, with stays like Phi Phi Island Cabana and PP Princess · Laem Tong, Loh Bagao, Long Beach and Loh Moo Dee are the quiet, calm side with clear water for snorkelling, needing a boat transfer but trading it for privacy, with stays like SAii, Phi Phi Holiday, Paradise Pearl, Viking and Phi Phi The Beach · choose the village zone if you want to party and explore on foot, and the quiet side if you want to relax

faq.q: ❓ Does Koh Phi Phi have both luxury and light-budget stays?
faq.a: It has both · the most luxurious is SAii Phi Phi Island Village, a 5-star resort on a private bay, starting around ฿6,000 · and there are still plenty of light-budget options, like Viking Nature Resort from ฿1,000 (treehouses/fan bungalows), Paradise Pearl ฿1,500 and Phi Phi Bayview ฿1,300 · what's interesting is that on Phi Phi the stays with the highest review scores are actually great-value beachfront bungalows, not the expensive resorts · choose by budget and check the real reviews before booking

faq.q: ❓ When is the best time to visit Koh Phi Phi?
faq.a: The time with the calmest seas, finest weather and clearest water for snorkelling is high season, November–April, good for snorkelling over coral, a trip to Maya Bay and a boat ride around Koh Phi Phi Leh, but prices are high and rooms fill fast, so book ahead · during May–October (low season) there's more rain and stronger waves, and some boat services stop, but prices drop and there are fewer people · Maya Bay closes for nature recovery in some years, so check the latest announcement before planning

faq.q: ❓ Is Koh Phi Phi worth staying overnight, or is a day trip enough?
faq.a: If you have the time, an overnight stay is far more worth it · a day trip catches the island when it's most crowded and Maya Bay is at its busiest · but people who stay overnight get to see the island in the morning and evening once the tour boats have gone, with quiet beaches, clear water and easy snorkelling right off the stay · accommodation on Phi Phi is limited and hard to reach, so it fills fast in high season — we recommend booking 1–2 months ahead and comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com, since each site often has different prices at different times
